slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use 5.1.2 Understanding Integer Division and Modulus as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Integer division truncates toward zero. The remainder operator % gives the corresponding remainder for integer operands. For nonnegative quantities, items / capacity counts complete groups and items % capacity counts leftover items. Require a positive capacity before either operation. Negative operands need extra care because remainder is not a universally nonnegative mathematical modulo. Also avoid the signed minimum divided by -1 when the positive result is not representable. These are representation constraints, not formatting problems. In the book’s grouping example, restricting the domain to nonnegative items and positive capacity keeps the arithmetic aligned with its physical meaning and avoids irrelevant negative-group interpretations. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use 5.2.1 Using Relational Operators as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Relational operators such as <, <=, >, and >= compare values; equality uses ==, not assignment’s =. A comparison produces a Boolean result. Write an interval test as low <= value && value <= high. The mathematical-looking low <= value <= high instead compares the first Boolean result with high and usually does not express the intended interval. Boundary decisions deserve explicit tests. Does a limit include its endpoint? Is an empty interval allowed? Are units compatible? Two numbers can be legally compared by the language while describing unrelated quantities. Domain types introduced later can prevent some of those comparisons at compile time; until then, names and validation must carry that meaning. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use 5.2.2 Combining Conditions with Logical Operators as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. && means logical and, || means logical or, and ! negates a logical value. The built-in && and || operators short-circuit: the second operand is evaluated only when needed. This allows a guard such as capacity != 0 && items / capacity > 2, though separating validation from calculation can be clearer. Do not substitute bitwise & or | for logical operators. They have different purposes and do not provide the same short-circuit protection. Keep conditions free of unnecessary assignments or increments. A condition that only observes state is easier to reuse, negate, and test than one that also consumes input or changes a counter. slides.title: 5.3.1 Understanding Precedence and Associativity
keyPoints: Precedence determines how operators group syntactically; associativity resolves grouping among operators at the.
Multiplication binds more tightly than addition, so a + b * c groups as a + (b * c).
Parentheses make a different grouping explicit and can also document intent when a reader might hesitate.
Precedence determines how operators group syntactically; associativity resolves grouping among operators at the.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use 5.3.1 Understanding Precedence and Associativity as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Precedence determines how operators group syntactically; associativity resolves grouping among operators at the same precedence level. Multiplication binds more tightly than addition, so a + b * c groups as a + (b * c). Parentheses make a different grouping explicit and can also document intent when a reader might hesitate. Grouping is not a general guarantee about the order in which every operand is evaluated. That distinction matters when operands have side effects. Instead of memorizing a large precedence table as a substitute for clarity, use a small set of familiar expressions and parenthesize less-obvious combinations. The compiler does not reward dense punctuation with better semantics. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use A small proof before execution as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. For nonnegative items and positive capacity, the quotient accounts for as many complete groups as possible. The remainder is smaller than the capacity. If it is zero, the quotient already covers every item. Otherwise, exactly one more group is sufficient because fewer than one group’s worth remains. That reasoning explains both branches of the final expression. It also identifies useful tests: an empty input, fewer items than capacity, an exact multiple, and one more than an exact multiple. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 5, use Failure clinic — Widening too late as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Imagine computing a large product in int and assigning it to long long. A reviewer sees the wide destination and assumes the calculation is safe. The multiplication may already have occurred in the narrower type. Inspect the operands, not only the destination. The same lesson applies to an overflow-prone numerator in a ceiling-division formula. A mathematically equivalent expression can have different intermediate range requirements. Good C++ arithmetic reasoning includes those intermediate states. This is why the book’s selected design favors a slightly longer quotient-and-remainder calculation over a compact formula with a hidden addition risk.
